[PMID: 42844043] Title: Impact of ALK rearrangement on survival in resected lung adenocarcinoma: A real-world analysis.
Abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic significance of ALK rearrangement after curative-intent resection of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains uncertain. Although the ALINA trial established adjuvant alectinib for resected ALK-positive NSCLC, patients with contemporary stage IA-IB disease were not fully represented. We evaluated stage-stratified outcomes of ALK-rearranged lung adenocarcinoma within an EGFR-excluded framework. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients undergoing curative-intent resection from 2005 to 2020. ALK status was determined using a two-step immunohistochemistry algorithm (p80/D5F3), and EGFR-mutant tumors were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:2) was used to balance clinicopathologic characteristics. Overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were compared according to ALK status and pathologic stage. RESULTS: Among 554 eligible patients, matching yielded 52 ALK-positive and 104 ALK-negative patients. In the matched cohort, OS and DFS did not differ significantly according to ALK status (p = 0.161 and p = 0.860, respectively). ALK rearrangement was not independently associated with OS (aHR, 0.584; 95% CI, 0.225-1.513) or DFS (aHR, 1.183; 95% CI, 0.562-2.489). In stage IA-IB disease, DFS was comparable (p = 0.602), while OS was numerically higher in the ALK-positive group but not statistically significant (p = 0.092). In stage II-III disease, neither OS nor DFS differed significantly by ALK status (p = 0.822 and p = 0.317, respectively). CONCLUSION: ALK rearrangement was not independently associated with postoperative OS or DFS. Patients with stage IA-IB disease demonstrated favorable long-term outcomes, whereas those with stage II-III disease remained at substantial risk of recurrence. These findings suggest that postoperative risk stratification should primarily consider pathologic stage rather than ALK status alone.

[PMID: 42837088] Title: Real-world evolution of first-line ALK-positive NSCLC management in Spain.
Abstract: OBJECTIVE: To describe real-world management of patients with ALK-positive advanced or metastatic NSCLC receiving first-line therapy in Spain, and to assess shifts in treatment patterns following the pricing and reimbursement of lorlatinib for first-line treatment in Spain. METHODS: This retrospective, cross-sectional analysis used data from the IQVIA Oncology Dynamics™ database. Patients with ALK-positive advanced or metastatic NSCLC receiving first-line treatment in Spain were included in two cohorts: before (July 2021-June 2022) and after (July 2024-June 2025) lorlatinib introduction. Patient characteristics, molecular profiles, and treatment patterns were described using descriptive statistics. RESULTS: A total of 342 patients were included. Patient characteristics were generally comparable across cohorts, although a higher disease burden and increased frequency of brain metastases were observed over time. A marked shift in treatment patterns was reported, with lorlatinib use increasing from 2 to 46% and becoming the most frequently prescribed first-line therapy in the later cohort, while alectinib use decreased from 85 to 41%. Among newly treated patients, lorlatinib accounted for 67% of prescriptions in the later cohort. Uptake of next-generation sequencing for molecular testing increased, and radiotherapy use declined over time. CONCLUSIONS: The management of ALK-positive NSCLC in Spain has evolved following the pricing and reimbursement of lorlatinib for first-line treatment in Spain, with changes in treatment selection and molecular testing practices observed in routine clinical settings.

[PMID: 42832145] Title: Limited Impact of Adjuvant Chemotherapy in ALK-Positive Stage II-III Lung Adenocarcinoma: A Multicenter CReGYT-03 ALK Study.
Abstract: BACKGROUND: Alectinib was approved in 2024 as an adjuvant therapy for resected ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) based on the ALINA trial. However, the role of cytotoxic adjuvant chemotherapy in this molecular subset remains uncertain. We evaluated the prognostic impact of cytotoxic adjuvant chemotherapy according to ALK status in patients with stage II-III lung adenocarcinoma. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 793 patients with pathologic stage II -III lung adenocarcinoma without EGFR mutations who underwent complete resection at 27 Japanese institutions. After propensity score matching (PSM) and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), we compared survival outcomes between the patients who received and did not receive cytotoxic adjuvant chemotherapy in the unadjusted cohort. Recurrence-free survival (RFS), overall survival (OS), and cumulative incidence of recurrence (CIR) were assessed. RESULTS: In ALK-negative disease, cytotoxic adjuvant chemotherapy significantly improved RFS, OS, and CIR, both before and after PSM (unadjusted: RFS hazard ratio [HR] 0.67; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.56-0.81; OS HR 0.55; 95% CI 0.43-0.71; CIR HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.61-0.90); similar favorable trends were observed after IPTW adjustment. Conversely, in ALK-positive disease, only OS showed a significant improvement in the unadjusted analysis (HR 0.19; 95% CI 0.04-0.81), whereas RFS and CIR did not differ significantly. After PSM and IPTW adjustment, similar overall trends were observed. CONCLUSIONS: The prognostic impact of cytotoxic adjuvant chemotherapy differed by ALK status, suggesting limited efficacy in ALK-positive adenocarcinoma and supporting tailored postoperative strategies for this subset.

text: Alectinib is a highly selective, second-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) that functions by binding to the ATP-binding pocket of the ALK fusion protein, thereby preventing the phosphorylation and subsequent activation of downstream oncogenic signaling pathways such as PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK. In ALK-positive NSCLC, this inhibition effectively suppresses the constitutive kinase activity driven by ALK rearrangements, leading to the inhibition of tumor cell proliferation and the induction of apoptosis. Recent clinical evidence, such as the ALINA trial, has validated the efficacy of this targeted approach in the adjuvant setting for resected ALK-positive NSCLC, although real-world management is currently evolving with the introduction of newer-generation inhibitors like lorlatinib [PMID: 42844043, PMID: 42837088, PMID: 42832145].
